headline: Midterms, Iran talks and a Bank of Canada hike dominate the week
summary: The Bank of Canada raised its rate to 2.50% as oil stayed above US$100, Ontario's deficit grew to $16.9 billion, and Iran talks and U.S. midterms ended the week on edge. Oil fell on Nov. 2 on hopes of a deal as voters went to the polls.

top.headline: Democrats gain in U.S. midterms; control of Congress still being counted
top.what: Counting continues, with early reports of Democratic gains and Trump saying he accepts the results.
top.why: It decides whether Trump's tariffs and war powers face a check.

top.headline: Oil falls on hopes of an Iran breakthrough after limited U.S. strikes
top.what: Brent dropped over 6% to US$105.55 after ending October near US$113 as mediators pushed a deal.
top.why: Oil prices drive fuel and inflation in Canada.

top.headline: Bank of Canada hikes to 2.50% as economy stalls
top.what: The bank made its first hike since 2023, then StatCan showed August growth flat.
top.why: Mortgage and loan costs rise into a weak economy.

top.headline: Canada-U.S. trade talks continue as tariffs stay
top.what: Carney reported a good call with Trump while the U.S. reshuffled its 50% tariff list.
top.why: Ontario factory jobs depend on steel and auto relief.

top.headline: Ontario's deficit swells to $16.9 billion
top.what: The fall update shows $36 billion in deficits over three years and matches Ottawa's investment write-off.

top.headline: Federal budget Thursday to include immigration levels update
top.what: Champagne tables Budget 2026 on Nov. 5 with small-business tax changes expected.
top.why: It sets Ottawa's fiscal and immigration direction.

top.headline: Bridle Path home invasion probe continues
top.what: Toronto police say there was no failure after a wanted man visited a hospital with a gunshot wound.
top.why: It raised questions about police coordination.

top.headline: GTA gas prices set for 11-cent drop Wednesday
top.what: Regular is forecast to fall 11 cents a litre, the biggest drop in months.
